panels.figure_caption: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (AITL). (A–C) – Hematoxylin-eosin (HE), optical microscopy, magnifications of 10 x (A), 20 x (B) and 40 x (C). Proliferation of small/medium sized atypical lymphoid cells diffusely infiltrating the lymph node with marked vascular proliferation. (D) high-rate of cell proliferation index - positive Ki-67 in more than 80% of the nuclei of atypical lymphoid cells. (E) Strong and diffuse labeling for the pan-T CD3 antigen. (F) Rare large CD20-positive cells in the paracortical region (“immunoblasts”). (G) CD4-positive in most neoplastic cells. (H) CD8-negative in neoplastic cells and positive in rare small reactive lymphocytes. (I) CD30-positive in large, expanded cells in the paracortical region with RS-like morphology. (J) Exuberant vascular proliferation with high endothelial venules (VEA) enhanced by CD34. (K) Expanded follicular dendritic cell (FDC) meshwork, labeling for CD21. (L) BCL6 positive and (M) CD10 positive, both markers of TFH origin. (N, O) In situ hybridization (ISH) for EBV, positivity for EBERs (Epstein-Barr small encoded-RNAs), staining in black, “speckled” pattern, revealing EBV staining in RS-like immunoblasts in the paracortex. (D–F, H, L–N) – Optical microscopy, 10 x magnification. (I, J, O) – Optical microscopy, 20 x magnification; (K) – Optical microscopy, 40 x magnification.
in_text_mentions: a cutaneous tumor infiltration by AITL (77). In the bone marrow, neoplastic infiltration by AITL can be characterized by nodular lymphoid infiltrates of paratrabecular or interstitial distribution, commonly accompanied by trilineage dysplasia, fibrosis, and plasmacytosis. TFH-associated markers usually have a lower yield in the bone marrow than in the lymph nodes, possibly due to impaired antigenic recovery influenced by sample decalcification (2, 77). Figures 2 , 3 summarize the main histological and immunohistochemical findings observed in classic cases of AITL in lymph node and bone marrow.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a double immunohistochemistry image of human AITL tissue showing PAX5-negative neoplastic lymphoid cells forming aggregates, a specific histologic manifestation of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. B: Panel B shows human AITL tissue with aggregates of medium-sized ROQUIN-positive neoplastic cells co-expressing the T follicular helper marker PD1, supporting the diagnosis of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.
panels.attribution_text: Auguste et al. ROQUIN/RC3H1 alterations are not found in angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.. PloS one 2013. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0064536. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Immunohistochemical detection of ROQUIN in AITL. Among the many cells showing a cytoplasmic granular staining for ROQUIN (brown), a few are PAX5-positive large cells (B-immunoblasts) (pink arrow) whereas most of them are small to medium-sized PAX5-negative lymphoid cells forming small aggregates, corresponding to neoplastic cells of AITL (black arrows) (A). In addition, these aggregates of medium-sized ROQUIN- positive cells (brown, granular staining) co expressed the TFH-associated marker PD1 (red, membrane staining) (B). Double immunohistochemistry, original magnification ×250.

in_text_mentions: ts had nodal infiltration (6 patients had nodal infiltration alone, and 17 patients had both nodal and extranodal infiltration). No patient had extranodal infiltration alone. Lymphoma lesions showed positive uptake of 18F-FDG (Figures 1 and 2). The distribution of 18F-FDG PET/CT in AITL patients with nodal infiltration was as follows: (i) multiple lymph nodes with scattered distribution were observed in 21 patients and (ii) localized distribution: only 2 patients were affected by diaphragmatic ipsilateral lymph nodes, including abdominopelvic cavity, retroperitoneum, and iliac vascular region.

in_text_mentions: mph node parenchyma was predominantly effaced and replaced by a lymphoid proliferation arranged in diffuse sheets of medium-sized cells with irregularly contoured, hyperchromatic, round nuclei and clear cytoplasm. These cells exhibited an immunoblastic appearance in some areas, characterized by increased cell size. The tumor cells were embedded in a polymorphic inflammatory background of lymphocytes, plasma cells, neutrophils, eosinophils, and histiocytes, with associated hyperplasia of vascular structures. Peripheral infiltration of the adipose tissue by tumor cells was also noted (Figure 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: H&E lymph node biopsy from the AITL case shows effacement of nodal architecture, medium-sized atypical lymphocytes, and high endothelial venules, matching AITL histology. B: CD23 immunostaining shows expanded follicular dendritic cell meshworks, a characteristic AITL finding. C: CD3 immunostaining demonstrates the T-cell lineage of the neoplastic infiltrate in this AITL lymph node biopsy. D: CD4 immunostaining is strongly positive in the neoplastic T cells, consistent with the AITL T-helper phenotype. E: PD-1 immunostaining is positive in the AITL lymph node biopsy, supporting the follicular helper T-cell phenotype. F: CXCL13 immunostaining shows focal positivity in the AITL lymph node biopsy, a marker of follicular helper T-cell derivation.

in_text_mentions: Regular histology revealed effacement of the normal lymph node architecture by a vaguely nodular to diffuse, tumour-cell rich lymphoid infiltrate with focal sparing of peripheral cortical sinuses and destruction of the lymph node capsule. An abundance of high endothelial venules was noted (Figure 1A). The neoplastic cells consisted of medium sized atypical lymphocytes with slightly eccentrically located nuclei with coarse chromatin. The mitotic count was elevated (>30/10 high power fields, HPF).

munochemistry revealed the neoplastic cells to be of a T-cell origin with positivity for CD2, CD3, CD4 and CD5, expression of PD1 (moderate staining intensity) and focal positivity for CXCL13 (Figure 1B-H); there was antigenic loss for CD7. Furthermore the cells strongly and diffusely expressed CD20, but no other B-cell markers (CD79a, CD19 and PAX5), which stained intermingled reactive small B-lymphocytes and scattered immunoblasts. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E section of the patient's excisional left inguinal lymph node biopsy showing diffuse effacement of the follicular/nodal architecture, a core histologic feature of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma in a case explicitly titled as AITL. B: Higher-power H&E of the same AITL lymph node demonstrating prominent (arborizing) vessels surrounded by sheets of neoplastic lymphoid cells, a hallmark of AITL. C: High-power (400x) H&E of the patient's AITL lymph node showing immunoblasts within the neoplastic infiltrate; immunoblasts are not represented in the supplied vocabulary, so they are proposed as findings. D: CD3 immunostain of the patient's lymph node showing sheets of T-cell (CD3-positive) lymphoma cells, supporting the T-cell lineage of the AITL infiltrate; CD3 positivity is not in the vocabulary, so it is proposed.

findings.label: Follicular dendritic cell meshwork on immunostaining
findings.evidence: Positive staining with anti-CD23 antibody, highlighting dendritic follicular cell networks

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (a, b, c, d, e). a: Panel a is an immunohistochemistry image from a patient with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, showing CD20-positive immunoblastic cells as captioned; this is a recognized immunophenotypic feature but is less specific than the T-cell markers. b: Panel b shows diffuse CD3 positivity in tumor cells, supporting a T-cell neoplasm in the setting of the captioned angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. c: Panel c demonstrates partial loss of CD7 expression, an aberrant T-cell immunophenotype characteristic of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. d: Panel d shows CD23-positive follicular dendritic cell networks, a well-recognized histologic feature of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. e: Panel e shows PD1 positivity in perifollicular T cells, consistent with the neoplastic T-follicular helper cell population seen in angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma.
panels.attribution_text: Salhi et al. Pleuropneumonia Revealing Angioimmunoblastic T-cell Lymphoma.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.80268. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. (a) Positive staining of immunoblastic cells with anti-CD20 antibodies. (b) Diffuse positive staining of tumor cells by anti-CD3 antibodies. (c) Partial loss of CD7 expression. (d) Positive staining with anti-CD23 antibody, highlighting dendritic follicular cell networks. (e) PD1 is positive in the perifollicular T cells PD-1: programmed cell death protein 1
in_text_mentions: munohistochemical analysis revealed diffuse positive staining of tumor cells with anti-CD3, anti-CD5, anti-BCL6, anti-CD2, anti-CD4, and anti-PD1 antibodies, along with partial loss of CD7 expression. Immunoblastic cells exhibited positive staining with anti-CD20 and anti-CD30 antibodies, while tumor cells showed focal labeling with the anti-CD10 antibody. The anti-CD23 antibody highlighted follicular dendritic cell networks, and histiocytes showed reactive labeling with the anti-CD68 antibody. In contrast, tumor cells did not stain with anti-CD15, anti-BCL2, or anti-CD8 antibodies (Figure 5).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: CD4 immunohistochemistry on lymph node from a patient with AITL, showing the characteristic CD4-positive atypical T-follicular helper cell infiltrate. b: EBER in situ hybridization on lymph node from a patient with AITL, highlighting scattered EBV-positive immunoblasts, a typical feature of AITL. c: Ki67 immunohistochemistry on lymph node from a patient with AITL, showing a proliferation index of 20-30% within the neoplastic T-cell population. d: CD30 immunohistochemistry on lymph node from a patient with AITL, highlighting scattered CD30-positive immunoblasts, a recognized feature of AITL.

plate_findings.evidence: Multiple mediastinal and abdominal lymphadenopathies with central necrosis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial abdominopelvic CT of an AITL patient showing enlarged abdominal/pelvic lymph nodes with necrotic centers, a recognized manifestation of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. B: Axial pelvic CT with red arrow indicating an enlarged iliac/abdominal lymph node with central necrosis in an AITL patient, consistent with AITL lymphadenopathy. C: Axial pelvic CT with red arrow pointing to a necrotic lymph node, demonstrating AITL-related abdominal lymphadenopathy. D: Coronal reformatted abdominopelvic CT showing multiple enlarged, centrally necrotic lymph nodes in an AITL patient, supporting AITL lymphadenopathy.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal chest CT (June 2021) from a case report on recurrence of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma; circled left axillary lymphadenopathy, a recognized AITL manifestation per the article's comparison of nodal disease over time. B: Coronal chest CT (April 2022) showing interval increase in circled axillary lymphadenopathy in a patient with recurrent angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma; caption and in-text explicitly describe the axillary nodal enlargement. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: H&E of the patient's right cervical lymph node showing the diagnostic AITL pattern of arborizing high endothelial venules with surrounding pale/clear atypical cells, matching the caption and article diagnosis of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. B: CD3 immunostaining of the patient's cervical lymph node demonstrating a T-cell lineage infiltrate in a case of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. C: CD10 immunostaining of the patient's lymph node confirming a follicular helper T-cell phenotype typical of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma. D: CD20 immunostaining of the same patient's cervical lymph node showing only scattered B cells (negative in the atypical population), supporting the non-B-cell lineage of the infiltrate in this AITL case; the panel is patient tissue but contributes a negative marker rather than a positive manifestation.

panels.rationale: Axial thoracic CT of a real human patient from a case report titled 'Pleuropneumonia Revealing Angioimmunoblastic T-cell Lymphoma'; the in-text description attributes the heterogeneous triangular consolidation with air bronchogram and nodular consolidation, together with pleural effusion, to a lymphomatous (AITL) etiology. Pleural effusion is directly supported by the allowed vocabulary; consolidation, air bronchogram and lung collapse are not in the vocabulary and are proposed. Pulmonary/pleural presentation as the revealing manifestation is atypical for AITL. No age, ethnicity or skin data provided.

in_text_mentions: Imaging studies provided further insights. A chest X-ray (Figure 1) showed moderate left-sided pleurisy, while a chest CT scan (Figure 2) highlighted a heterogeneous triangular consolidation in the left upper lung parenchyma. This lesion was characterized by an air bronchogram and nodular areas of consolidation. The CT scan also revealed bilateral bronchopneumonic infiltrates, which strongly suggested a lymphomatous etiology.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 9 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I). A: Clinical photograph of the AITL patient's skin lesions (erythema with hemorrhagic bullae/vasculitis-like ulcers) that led to the diagnosis; the article is a case report of AITL and the caption/in-text attribute these lesions to this patient's disease. The ulcero-bullous morphology is an unusual (non-specific) skin presentation, hence atypical. B: Second clinical view of the same AITL patient's skin lesions (scattered erythematous lesions with hemorrhagic crusts) on the trunk/limbs, attributed to AITL in this case report; morphology is a non-specific/atypical cutaneous presentation of AITL. C: Third clinical view of the AITL patient's truncal skin involvement (diffuse erythema with residual pigmented/healed lesions); disease attribution rests on the case-report context plus the captioned skin manifestation, which is a non-specific (atypical) AITL skin presentation. in_text_mentions: Two months after her first visit to the ED, she began experiencing dyspnea, left pleuritic chest pain, and worsening dry cough while maintaining the previous fever pattern. A subsequent CT scan showed an enlargement in the size and number of adenopathies and hepatosplenomegaly (Figure 2). Because of the urgent need to elucidate the clinical presentation and respiratory failure, the patient was admitted. She underwent an incisional biopsy of a cervical lymph node, revealing eosinophilic infiltration, areas of necrosis, granulomas, activated B-cells, and inconclusive T-cell clonality.

in_text_mentions: Scan of the neck, chest, and abdomen obtained nine days after admission revealed diffuse lymphadenopathy (cervical, mediastinal, retroperitoneal, and pelvic) and no hepatosplenomegaly. A biopsy of the skin lesions on the posterior chest and an excisional cervical lymph node biopsy revealed angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma (AITL) with cutaneous involvement (Figures 3 and 4). Later, the patient went into respiratory failure. Given his deteriorating clinical status at the time of diagnosis, he was not a candidate for chemotherapy. Sadly, he died within a week from sepsis and multiorgan failure.

panels.figure_caption: The histology and immunohistochemistry of a lymph node. (a) Gross examination of the lymph node architecture shows prominent vessels, suggesting the formation of the arborizing high endothelial venules. (b) The expanded CD21-positive follicular dendritic cell meshworks. (c) Hematoxylin and eosin stain showing polymorphous background infiltrate composed of medium sized atypical lymphocytes and enlarged pleomorphic cells with unilobated nuclei and prominent nucleoli, resembling RS-like B-cells. (d) The RS-like B-cells have less prominent CD20 expression in comparison to the B-lymphocytes present in the polymorphous infiltrate. (e) The RS-like B-cells are CD30-positive with characteristic paranuclear dot-like staining. (f) The lymphoid population consists of the CD2-positive atypical T-lymphocytes that often form rosettes around RS-like B-cells. (g) and (h) Atypical T-lymphocytes are CD10- and BCL6-positive.

Microscopic examination revealed effacement of the normal nodular architecture with predominantly small-sized lymphoid cells with cleaved nuclei and scant cytoplasm distributed among a polymorphous background infiltrate including small lymphocytes, eosinophils, plasma cells, and histiocytes (Figure 1(c)). Enlarged cells resembling Hodgkin-like cells or RS-like B-cells with abundant pale cytoplasm and unilobated and enlarged nuclei with prominent eosinophilic nucleoli were noticed (Figure 1(c)). Evident proliferation of arborizing high endothelial venules was observed (Figure 1(a)).

Immunohistological analyses demonstrated a diffuse increase in CD3-positive T-lymphocytes that were also CD2-, CD4-, and CD5-positive (Figure 1(f)). Atypical T-lymphocytes were CD10- and B-cell lymphoma 6- (BCL6-) positive, indicative of T-follicular helper (TFH) phenotype (Figures 1(g) and 1(h)). marked interstitial infiltration of small lymphocytes with cleaved nuclei and scant cytoplasm (in-text)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: H&E bone marrow biopsy from a patient with AITL showing prominent lymphoid infiltration, consistent with bone marrow involvement. b: CD3 immunohistochemistry demonstrating atypical T-lymphocytes in bone marrow, supporting AITL marrow involvement. c: CD20 immunohistochemistry showing RS-like B-cells in bone marrow from an AITL patient, a recognized less common finding. d: CD30 immunohistochemistry highlighting RS-like B-cells with dot-like paranuclear staining in bone marrow, a variant feature in AITL.
panels.attribution_text: Willemsen et al. A Rare Case of Angioimmunoblastic T-Cell Lymphoma with Epstein-Barr Virus-Negative Reed-Sternberg-Like B-Cells, Chylous Ascites, and Chylothorax.. Case reports in hematology 2017. doi:10.1155/2017/1279525. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histology and immunohistochemistry of bone marrow. (a) Hypercellular bone marrow with prominent lymphoid infiltration. (b) Atypical CD3-positive T-lymphocytes. (c) Enlarged pleomorphic cells with unilobated nuclei and prominent nucleoli, resembling RS-like B-cells. These cells show less pronounced expression of CD20 compared to normal B-lymphocytes (a CD20-positive small cell population in the background). (d) The RS-like B-cells are CD30-positive with characteristic paranuclear dot-like staining.
in_text_mentions: The premortal bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellularity with marked interstitial infiltration of small lymphocytes with cleaved nuclei and scant cytoplasm (Figure 3(a)). These lymphocytes were CD3-positive and were organized in paratrabecular clusters together with a high number of CD68-positive histiocytes and eosinophils (Figure 3(b)). The CD20- and CD30-positive RS-like B-cells were distributed within this population (Figures 3(c) and 3(d)). EBER-ISH was negative (Figure 2).

On the basis of a left-side axillary lymph node biopsy specimen, he was diagnosed with AITL (Fig. 1a), and then the patient came to our department for treatment. We performed a detailed physical examination but only found bilateral cervical multiple lymphadenopathy without fever, cough, chest tightness, and edema. His laboratory test abnormal findings were as follows: red blood cell count, 3.76 × 1012/L; hemoglobin, 7.5 g/dl; aspartate transaminase/alanine transaminase ratio, 2.12 (normal rang

ut 13 × 10 mm. Histopathological study was performed again and indicated AITL, which showed small to medium-sized lymphocytes, transparent cytoplasm, and vascular hyperplasia in the lymph nodes (Fig. 1b). The results of immunohistochemistry were as follows: CD34+, CD4+, CD38+, Bcl-6+, CD21+, CD20+, CD23+, CD5+, CD10−, PD-1+, and Ki-67 (50%). On the basis of these findings, a diagnosis of AITL was made, and the staging of lymphoma was IIIA. source_variant.context: The patient developed an annular plaque on the leg (A). A biopsy was obtained and was held to be consistent with angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma (B-F). The biopsy exhibited an atypical perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate characterized by pleomorphic small-to-intermediate–sized noncerebriform atypical lymphocytes. Epidermotropism was also noted (C). The phenotypic profile was characteristic for angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, whereby the lymphocytes stained for CD2 (D), establishing their T-cell lineage, CD4 (E), and exhibited follicular helper T-cell marker-positivity, including BCL6 (F) and PD1 (G).

International journal of molecular sciences 2022. doi:10.3390/ijms23169349. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Immunohistochemistry of the FDC component. Pale fascicles and nodules ((A) H&E) of FDCs were highlighted by both CD21 (B) and CD23 (C) stainings (o.m. ×5). CD30 ((D) o.m. ×5) stained sparse medium/large lymphocytes ((E) CD30 o.m. ×200), mainly of the T-cell lineage ((F) CD3, o.m. ×200) as shown by the rarity of the B cells ((G) CD79a o.m. ×200), and numerous FDC ((H) CD30 o.m. ×100; ((I) CD21 o.m. ×100). The Ki-67 index ((K) o.m. ×5) in the FDC areas was about 40%; ((J) o.m. ×100).
in_text_mentions: had a T immunophenotype (CD3+, CD5+, CD4+) with partial loss of CD7 and expression of the TFH markers CD10, BCL6, and PD1 (Figure 2A–H), whereas the pale areas were composed of CD23+ and CD21+ FDCs (Figure 3A–C). Intermixed to these two components, there was a polymorphous inflammatory background containing variable amounts of reactive small cytotoxic -cells (CD8+, TIA1+, Granzyme B+) (Figure 2I), scattered CD20+ and CD79a+ B lymphocytes, rare CD138+ polytypic plasma cells (Figure 2J), histiocytes, and eosinophils. A high proliferation index was demonstrated by staining for Ki67 (Figure 2K).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of lymph node from a patient with AITL shows architectural effacement with alternating pale and dark zones, a classic AITL histologic pattern. B: Medium-power H&E of an AITL lymph node dark area showing atypical clear-cytoplasm lymphocytes and HEV association. C: High-power H&E of AITL lymph node showing atypical clear/eosinophilic T cells with perinodal adipose extension, typical of AITL. D: High-power H&E of AITL lymph node pale area showing whorls of spindled/ovoid cells around capillaries with mitotic figures; supports the exuberant follicular dendritic cell proliferation described in the article.

panels.figure_caption: Histology of the lymph nodes. Pale and dark areas were evident at even low magnification ((A) hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) original magnification (o.m.) ×16, insert o.m. ×5; (B) H&E o.m. ×66). The dark areas were populated by atypical lymphocytes with clear cytoplasm clustered around HEVs and infiltrating the perinodal adipose tissue (insert). Admixed small lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils were also present ((C) H&E o.m. ×200; insert ×200). The pale areas were composed of whorls of proliferating spindled and ovoid cells arranged around blood capillaries ((D) H&E o.m. ×200; blue arrows indicate mitotic figures).

findings.evidence: enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Axial fused PET/CT of the abdomen showing enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes with increased FDG uptake, a classic nodal manifestation of AITL in this biopsy-proven case report. B: Pelvic PET/CT from the staging study of the same AITL patient showing mildly increased FDG metabolism without bone destruction; disease-related hypermetabolism, though the specific involved structure is not clearly delineated. C: Fused PET/CT of the neck demonstrating enlarged, FDG-avid cervical lymph nodes, a typical nodal presentation of AITL. D: Abdominal PET/CT showing an enlarged, hypermetabolic spleen, a classic extranodal manifestation of AITL in this case. E: Fused PET/CT at the level of the pelvis/inguinal regions showing bilateral enlarged, FDG-avid inguinal lymph nodes in the AITL patient. F: Thoracic fused PET/CT showing enlarged FDG-avid lymph nodes at the cardiophrenic angle, an additional nodal site of involvement in this...

panels.figure_caption: (A–C) Biopsy of left cervical lymph node showed effacement of architecture and diffuse hyperplasia of medium-large-sized heterogenous lymphocytes with oval nuclei and clear or faintly eosinophilic cytoplasm. The hyperplasia of HEV and plasma cells and infiltrates of eosinophils were also observed. The neoplastic cells were positive for Bcl-6 (D), CD3 (E) and PD-1 (I) in IHC. CD20 (F) stood for B cells and CD21 (G) labeled follicular dendritic cell meshwork. CXCL13 (H) was negative.
in_text_mentions: HEVs and plasma cells and infiltrates of eosinophils were also observed. The atypical medium-to-large cells were positive for CD3 and CD4. Some of these cells also exhibited BCL-6+ and PD-1+, indicating the phenotype of follicular helper T cell (TFH). Some scattered large immunoblasts were CD20-positive. The EBER in situ hybridization test was negative. CD21-positive cells were mainly located in the follicular dendritic cell meshwork. CD56, CXCL13 and CD10 were negative. Ki67 was 70% (Figure 4). The PCR+capillary electrophoresis revealed a positive for the rearrangement of IgH, TCRβ and TCRγ.

findings.label: Arborizing high endothelial venules
findings.evidence: Prominent vasculature with arborizing high endothelial venules is noted (red arrow)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of inguinal lymph node biopsy from a patient with confirmed AITL showing diffuse effacement of nodal architecture, a hallmark histologic feature of AITL. B: H&E panel explicitly captioned as arborizing high endothelial venules (red arrow), a classic diagnostic feature of AITL, from the same AITL lymph node biopsy. C: High-power H&E showing the pleomorphic medium-sized atypical lymphoid cells characteristic of the neoplastic infiltrate in AITL, from the confirmed AITL biopsy. D: High-power H&E of the AITL lymph node biopsy showing Reed-Sternberg-like binucleated atypical cells (asterisks), a recognized but less common morphologic variant within the AITL infiltrate; the underlying atypical large cells support AITL attribution.

panels.figure_caption: Inguinal lymph node biopsy (A) The lymph node architecture was largely effaced by a polymorphous lymphoid infiltrate. (B) Prominent vasculature with arborizing high endothelial venules is noted (red arrow). (C) Pleomorphic medium-sized cells with irregular nuclei, abundant pink cytoplasm, irregular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli. (D) Reed-Sternberg-like cells are also present (asterisks), with occasional binucleation.
in_text_mentions: Subsequently, low-molecular-weight heparin initially started on admission for thromboprophylaxis was discontinued. Workup revealed a negative heparin-induced thrombocytopenia panel and enlarged inguinal lymph nodes bilaterally. Inguinal lymph node biopsy showed AITL (Figures 3A-3D).
